children: Micron Technology, Inc. (NASDAQ:MU) reported robust fiscal Q3 results—$41.46B revenue and $18.3B adjusted FCF—driven by cloud and data‑center demand keeping DRAM/NAND tight while capacity waits until 2027–28, even as Taiwan union strike threats, mixed analyst moves and a court win shape near‑term risk.
Micron Q3 Revenue, Free Cash Flow
: Micron (MU) posted fiscal Q3 revenue $41.46B and adjusted free cash flow $18.3B. Cloud-memory sales $13.77B and data-center $11.52B — about 61% of revenue.
: Micron (MU): AI data-center demand keeps DRAM/NAND tight. Micron near capacity with Samsung and SK Hynix; Nvidia tied to long-term supply. New fab capacity not expected until late 2027–2028.
Micron Unions Demand Payout, Profit Share
: Taiwan unions of ~10,000 Micron (MU) workers demand a one‑time 2026 payout (~83 months’ pay) and a 2027 profit‑share plan allocating 15% of operating profit to quarterly bonuses; 80% backed strike.
: Analysts updated Micron (MU) price targets and ratings pre-earnings: Mizuho cut forecasts and target, New Street raised rating and target, Citigroup kept Buy but adjusted its target.
: U.S. appeals court affirmed Micron didn’t infringe Netlist’s DIMM patent. Ruling clears MU of alleged memory-system infringement; related Netlist stock plunged about 20% on the day.
: Micron (MU) trades above its 200-period SMA (~880) and is supported by SuperTrend (~907). MACD momentum has faded and ADX (~17) signals weak trend, raising false-breakout risk.
